final_message:
:** The atom-count check now uses a closed-form count of partial sums instead of computing them. The two counts were equal on the parent's laws. The search now takes 3.5 s per instance; the parent took 11.4 s, which was over the 5 s limit.
- **Atom budget:** I raised the verification budget from 1.5e6 to 2.0e6 ops. Certification now takes 9.6–11 s on this machine; the limit is 20 s. If the grading machine is about 1.8 times slower, the n=4 and n=6 instances will time out.
- **Confidence and header:** I added `confidence(c)`. It returns 0.01 when the limit model's value is more than 2e-4 above the certified value, and 0.3 if not. That gap rule gives 0.01 on all three train instances and all four test instances. I also wrote the 5-line header and `report.json`.

**Why I stopped:**
- Every candidate structure reduced to the same shape: one ladder below a centre, plus a scaled copy of the law at 0.
- The optimiser has converged. Giving it 12 s instead of 3.5 s changed the value by less than 3e-6.
- For c1_2_-3 I ran a free-position search at 8 and 12 atoms. It found nothing better than the lexicographic ladder, so 64 atoms is already the limit there.
- The remaining gap is the finite-ladder loss from coincident atoms, about 0.003–0.007. Only more atoms reduce it.
- Weight precision and denominator size had almost no effect on certification time, so they give no extra atoms.

I deleted my scratch copies of the parent code. `best.json` is from `check.py` and is still in the folder.
